name: Engineering Economics: Worthal
subtitle: Engineering Economics Course
shortDescription: Adaptive engineering economics course: time value of money, IRR, depreciation, risk and capital budgeting with five labs. Learning only.
longDescription:
Engineering Economics: Worthal is a practice course for the decisions engineers make with money over time. You type a number, the app checks it, and when the number matches a known slip it tells you which one: a nominal rate used as an effective rate, salvage value left out, the wrong count of periods, a factor turned upside down.

### What You Practise
- Time value of money, nominal and effective interest, cash-flow series and gradients
- Present, future and annual worth, rate of return, benefit-cost and payback
- Alternatives with unequal lives, depreciation (straight line, declining balance, 5-year MACRS), after-tax cash flow
- Inflation, break-even and sensitivity analysis, expected value and simulation, replacement analysis, capital budgeting

### How It Works
- Two paths: a personalised path that picks your next problem from spaced review and your recent slips, or the traditional topic order. Switch at any time.
- 228 original numeric problems and 26 practice-only concept questions, 16 topics, a worked solution beside every answer. Worked solutions are always free.
- Timed mock exams of ten numeric problems, with no ads during the exam.
- Concept pop-ups at three levels: school, early university, beyond the course.
- Citation sheets link the textbooks and course pages used as scope references.
- A-minus and A-plus text size buttons on every text screen.

### Five Interactive Labs
- Cash-flow timeline: place receipts and costs on a year ruler and watch present, future and annual worth, rate of return and payback update.
- Unequal-lives comparator: two machines, least common multiple or study-period horizon.
- Depreciation and tax: schedules, book value and the tax shield side by side.
- Break-even and tornado: see which input swings the result most.
- Monte Carlo: seeded trials, histogram, spread and chance of a loss.

### Free, Offline, No Account
The whole course works without an internet connection and without signing in. The app shows ads from Google AdMob at natural breaks, such as after you finish a set, never during a timed exam. On iPhone and iPad it asks for your permission before tracking and shows a consent form where required. You can also watch an optional short video to earn extra mock-exam credits.

### Ad-Free Subscription
Remove ads with Engineering Economics Ad-Free Monthly. The price is shown by the App Store before you subscribe. It includes a 7-day free trial, then renews automatically every month until cancelled. Payment is charged to your Apple ID at confirmation; the subscription renews unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the period. Manage or cancel it in Settings, under your name, then Subscriptions. Any unused part of a free trial ends when you subscribe. Restore Purchases is in the Me tab.

### For Learning Only
This app is for study. Its results are not financial, investment, tax or legal advice, and it is not affiliated with any exam, school or accrediting body.
